pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a good way to practise the shape of a letter? (1 mark)
   A. Cover it
   B. Rub it out
   C. Ignore it
   D. Trace it in the air with your finger

2. What is a singing game with interjections? (1 mark)
   A. A written test
   B. A silent game
   C. A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise
   D. A story

3. What is the problem in a story? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. The page
   C. The trouble or challenge the characters face
   D. The ending word

4. Which of these can begin a happy line? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck!
   B. Oh no!
   C. Hurray!
   D. Ouch!

5. What should you do if a stranger promises cheap goods and asks for money first? (1 mark)
   A. Send money at once
   B. Be careful and ask an adult
   C. Trust them
   D. Give your address

6. How can recording your reading help you? (1 mark)
   A. It ends practice
   B. You can listen back and see how to improve
   C. It makes you forget
   D. It deletes the story

7. What does A stitch in time saves nine mean? (1 mark)
   A. Stitches are costly
   B. Sewing is easy
   C. Fix small problems early
   D. Nine is a lucky number

8. Which of these is a safety rule from the road safety dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Look right, then left, then right again
   B. Play on the road
   C. Cross anywhere
   D. Run across without looking

9. A sentence always begins with (1 mark)
   A. a full stop
   B. a capital letter
   C. a number
   D. a comma

10. Which is a difference between an advert and a news item? (1 mark)
   A. An advert tries to sell and news reports facts
   B. Adverts report elections only
   C. News is always a poem
   D. They are exactly the same

11. What does legible writing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Writing very small
   B. Writing that can be read easily
   C. Writing with a red pen
   D. Writing in capital letters only

12. A newsreader on the radio should speak (1 mark)
   A. with no pauses
   B. in a whisper
   C. very fast
   D. clearly and at a steady pace

13. Why do we listen to oral texts about safety? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. To learn how to stay safe
   C. To sleep
   D. To count the words

14. What is creative writing? (1 mark)
   A. Writing only numbers
   B. Copying a text exactly
   C. Writing a list of names
   D. Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces

15. What is a good rule for handling library books? (1 mark)
   A. Turn pages gently and return them on time
   B. Write in them
   C. Leave them outside
   D. Fold the corners

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain when you would skim and when you would scan. Give one example of each. (5 marks)

17. Compose a four-line poem about leisure that includes two interjections. (5 marks)

18. Explain the difference in punctuation between Wow! and Oops, it is torn. (3 marks)

19. Give two features of a poem. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Trace it in the air with your finger
   Tracing helps the hand remember the movement.

2. C — A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise
   Interjections can be part of songs.

3. C — The trouble or challenge the characters face
   The problem drives the events.

4. C — Hurray!
   Hurray shows happiness.

5. B — Be careful and ask an adult
   Such offers may be tricks.

6. B — You can listen back and see how to improve
   Playing back shows where to improve.

7. C — Fix small problems early
   Early action prevents bigger trouble.

8. A — Look right, then left, then right again
   The dialogue teaches how to look before crossing.

9. B — a capital letter
   A capital letter shows the start of a sentence.

10. A — An advert tries to sell and news reports facts
   Their purposes differ.

11. B — Writing that can be read easily
   Legible means easy to read.

12. D — clearly and at a steady pace
   News should be clear and easy to follow.

13. B — To learn how to stay safe
   Safety texts teach what to do and what to avoid.

14. D — Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces
   Creative writing is imaginative.

15. A — Turn pages gently and return them on time
   Good care keeps books usable for others.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: Skim when you want the main idea, for example looking through an article. Scan when you want one fact, for example looking for a name on a list.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two situations and two marks for examples and one mark for correct meaning.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines about free time with two suitable interjections, for example Wow, it is time to play! Hurray, no lessons today! We run and read and sing, Free time is a lovely thing.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each line up to four and one mark for two suitable interjections.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: An exclamation mark shows strong feeling, and a comma after a mild interjection shows a softer feeling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each punctuation mark and one for the difference.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: Short lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, images (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
